newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA LEU ENDS DOWN, MARKET AWAITING C.BANK MOVE.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA LEU ENDS DOWN, MARKET AWAITING C.BANK MOVE.

text.p: Romania's leu closed Monday lower at 7,500/600 to the dollar after idling at 7,200/300 throughout the day with traders waiting for the central bank (BNR) to name the banks reauthorised to act as dealers.

"The funny thing is that some of us will be acting as dealers again tomorrow but we still don't know which of us as the central bank has failed to make any announcement so far," said one trader with a bank relegated to a broker status on the local market last March.
The BNR said last Friday several banks would get back their lost local dealer licences starting Tuesday. Over the past year the local market operated with only four dealers.
Most operators said trading kept a subdued note with few hard currency offers coming mainly from foreign investors on the local capital market.
But they said the market was still affected by squeezes, with hard currency holders awaiting weaker prices.
"I see the leu down at 8,000 in the next few days," said one trader.
Short-term rates went higher to some 130 percent for one-week funds on a money market plagued by leu shortages.

Traders said they were bracing for fresh news expected later on Monday when Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea sets forth a reform package which his centrist coalition government discussed with international lenders.
The government is seeking up to $1.0 billion in total loans from the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank, which had withheld credits to Romania last year.
